When Money Worry Won’t Switch Off

For the nights the numbers keep circling and nothing gets decided. It turns the vague dread into facts, one next step and a time to stop, so the worry has somewhere to go besides 3 am.

Money · Money · Worry · 8 items · whenever you need it

The checklist

  • Write the actual number down — A known figure is easier to face than the one your head keeps rounding up.
  • Separate this week from this year — Most money dread is a far-off problem borrowing tonight’s attention.
  • Name the very next step — One call, one form, one email; not the whole way out.
  • Give it a slot tomorrow — Worry lets go a little once it has an appointment.
  • Find out what help exists — Payment plans, hardship terms and free advice lines are more common than people think.
  • Tell one person the real picture — Money worry gets heavier in private than it ever is out loud.
  • Stop checking the balance tonight — Looking again after hours changes nothing and costs you the sleep.
  • Do one kind ordinary thing — Tea, a shower, a walk; being broke is not a reason to go without comfort.

Use this checklist Free account: tick items off and keep each day's record.

How to use it

Run through it whenever you need it, honestly and without scoring yourself. A checklist is a way of noticing, not a test: an item you cannot tick is information about the day, not a verdict on you. Over a few weeks the pattern of what gets ticked and what does not says more than any single pass.

With a free Theraglee account the checklist remembers each pass, so you can look back. Without one, you can still read it here and keep your own copy.

Checklists like this one

When a Bill You Cannot Pay Arrives For the letter or email that asks for money you do not have right now. It helps you find out what is actually owed and by when, make the call before… Putting the Phone Down Mid-Scroll For the half hour that disappears into bad news and other people's lives. It helps you notice you are scrolling, break the loop without deleting… Taking the Edge Off Sunday Night For the Sunday-evening slump, when the week ahead starts pressing in before it has even begun. The Week You Are Waiting on News For the stretch between a test, an application or a decision and the answer, when nothing you do changes the outcome.

Reading that goes with it

The Mail You Have Not Opened A pile of envelopes on the side, some of them official, one of them from the hospital. What If It Really Is as Bad as You Think Reassurance does not touch some worries. The alternative is to follow the fear to the end on purpose and ask what you would actually do. Living on Less Than You Used To Hours cut, a job lost, a separation, retirement. Adjusting downward is a practical problem and an identity one, and the second part is what makes it…
